before.tpp_requirement_evidence_tier: coefficient verified in yeast-GEM 9.1.1 on 2026-10-22; it is an S. cerevisiae value, not measured in Y. lipolytica, and is provisional. That TPP is a required cofactor (pyruvate dehydrogenase, 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase, transketolase, pyruvate decarboxylase) is established/uncited. m975 has no formula or cross-reference; its identity as thiamine diphosphate is inferred from its reactions R752 (KEGG R00619), R753 (KEGG R00616) and R933 (thiamine diphosphate transport).
before.tpp_requirement_rationale: No reaction drained cytosolic TPP (m975) to a sink: its consumers R753 (to thiamine triphosphate, m976) and R933 (into mitochondria, m1116) end in dead ends. So TPP synthesis and THI80 (R752) carried no flux and a THI80 knockout had no effect. Diluting TPP into new biomass makes its synthesis required, as yeast-GEM does for TDP.

after.trehalose_biomass_previous_term: m294[C_cy] trehalose at 0.00686 mmol/gDW (6.86 nmol/mg DW, 2.35 mg/gDW), inherited from the source model. The same number is hard-coded without a source in the eciYali5-GEM build script (xCARBOHYDRATE); it is the iYali4 xBIOMASS trehalose share (0.0032) scaled about 2.14 times with glucan, mannan and chitin. No Yarrowia lipolytica measurement behind it was found.
after.trehalose_biomass_evidence: Flores et al. 2011, PLoS One, PMID 21931609, PMC3171402 (full text): Y. lipolytica wild type contains below 1 nmol trehalose per mg dry weight in minimal glucose medium (Table 4; per Methods, YNB without amino acids and ammonium sulfate plus 0.1 percent glutamate, generally 2 percent glucose, 30 C), and below 1 when grown in glucose up to stationary phase or in glycerol. The tps1 disruptant (YlTPS1 = YALI0E14685g = YALI1E17616g, UniProt O74932, cDNA AJ011032) grows on glucose at least as fast as the wild type (doubling time 139 vs 149 min); no trehalose is detected in tps1 with nth1 also disrupted or after heat shock (the content of the single tps1 mutant at 30 C is not reported). Trehalose is therefore not an obligate biomass component under this condition. Report reports/trehalose_biomass_20261030.
after.trehalose_biomass_evidence_tier: direct Y. lipolytica measurement (an upper bound: reported as below 1 nmol/mg DW; the paper states no detection limit) plus a Y. lipolytica mutant phenotype; strain CJM 645 on YNB-glutamate glucose, not PO1f on the Task A medium; heat shock (not modelled) raises trehalose to 7-20 nmol/mg DW
after.trehalose_biomass_scope: Only the biomass_C trehalose term is removed; biomass_C is not re-normalised. The trehalose terms of the non-objective xBIOMASS, newBiom and R1372, the closed R1387 and R1710, and the R143 rule are unchanged.
